title: Right Hop Converter
description: Pin the unit you have and the unit you want, hop the point right one place at a time, and watch the number multiplied by 10 at each hop, with zeros dropping in to hold places.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Change a measure from a bigger unit to a smaller one by counting the places from the unit you have to the unit you want and multiplying the number by 10 for each, change a mixed measure bigger part first, keep the zeros that hold places, and write a long road in metres.
writeup.look: One row of the unit chart with digit tiles in its columns, two pins, a point that hops right, and grey zeros dropping into empty columns.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Right Hop Converter' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of hops the point has made. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. One row of the chart runs across the middle of the area at y 380: seven columns, each 140 wide, from x 90 to x 1070, headed kilo to milli with the base unit in the middle and the unit names violet, labelled Unit. The given measure stands in deep blue digit tiles, labelled Given, with the point in the gap after its unit. The deep blue have pin stands over the unit you have at y 300, and the green want pin is dragged along the same line. The Hop button stands at x 900, y 230, and each hop moves the point one gap to the right and draws a vermilion arrow under the row along y 470, labelled Move, multiply the number by 10. Each column the point passes that holds no digit gets a grey zero, labelled Place holder. On the second and third phases the smaller part's card waits at x 120, y 560 with the Add part button beside it at x 400, y 560, and the column being filled is amber. On the fourth phase the road sign hangs above the row at x 120, y 220, and a second sign appears beside it once the answer is in. The answer is read in green, labelled Answer, at x 120, y 660, with its unit. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a comma key for grouping and a delete key. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. The measure the question gives, in the unit it is given in, is deep blue, labelled Given or Measure. The measure the working reaches, and a reading on a scale, is green, labelled Answer, Reading or Same measure. The places moved across the unit chart, and the worth of one small mark on a scale, are vermilion, labelled Move or One mark. A unit fact, the unit names on the chart and the other temperature scale are violet, labelled Unit fact, Unit or Other scale. The part taken away, and a part left over after sharing, are rose, labelled Taken away or Left over. The unit, column, mark or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open inside a number, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. Rulers, tapes, jugs, scales, thermometer tubes, chart lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last measure stays on the row with its hops drawn beneath, its zeros in place and its answer in green with its unit.

phases.win: two grey zeros drop in behind the digit, and the grams turn green
phases.does: drags the want pin to g, counts the places, and hops the point right once for each
phases.goal: count the places from the unit you have to the unit you want; each place to the right multiplies the number by 10
phases.says: Pin the unit you want. Hop right once for each place.
phases.check: Away from the screen: from metres to centimetres, which way do you go, and how many places?
phases.feels: the point sliding right and zeros dropping in behind the digit
phases.hands: On the paper chart, write a weight in hectograms under hg. Put a coin on hg and another on g, count the steps, and move the paper point one column right for each, writing a zero in every column it passes.
phases.tries: First rung: count the places between the pins without hopping. Second rung: hop once and read the measure. Third rung: the same task between two neighbouring units, before the question's own measure returns.

wrong.why: a smaller unit sounds like it should give a smaller number
wrong.move: hops the point to the left instead of the right
wrong.screen: the point stays and the measure is read back in the unit it now sits after, far less than the card shows; the pins light amber and the places between them are counted again one hop at a time

wrong.why: zeros look like nothing, so they seem safe to leave off
wrong.move: types the digit and stops, with no zeros after it
wrong.screen: the columns the point passed are lit amber inside the answer, one at a time, each waiting for its grey zero

phases.screen: a weight in hectograms set in the row, the have pin on hg and the want pin loose
phases.soWhat: count the places from the unit you have to the unit you want; each place to the right multiplies the number by 10

phases.win: the two parts meet in one row, and the millilitres turn green
phases.does: hops the litres part into millilitres, then slides the millilitres part in with Add part
phases.goal: a mixed measure is changed bigger part first, then the smaller part is added
phases.says: Change the litres first. Then add the millilitres.
phases.check: Away from the screen: a bottle holds some litres and some millilitres. Which part do you change first?
phases.feels: two parts in two units meeting in one row as one number
phases.hands: Write a capacity in litres and millilitres on two cards. Change the litres card into millilitres on the paper chart first, then add the millilitres card to it.
phases.tries: First rung: change only the litres part. Second rung: add a millilitres part of three digits. Third rung: the same task on a length in metres and centimetres, before the question's own capacity returns.

wrong.why: both are numbers in the question, and adding is how two parts are joined
wrong.move: adds the litres number and the millilitres number as they stand
wrong.screen: the litres part is lit amber, still in litres, and it hops into millilitres in steps before the millilitres card slides in beside it, while the child's sum stays in the slot

wrong.why: the hop felt like the whole job
wrong.move: hops the litres part and types that as the answer
wrong.screen: the Add part button is lit amber, with the millilitres card still waiting beside it

phases.screen: a capacity in litres and millilitres, its litres part set in the row and its millilitres part waiting on a card
phases.soWhat: a mixed measure is changed bigger part first, then the smaller part is added
phases.concept: A mixed measure in the smaller unit

phases.win: a grey zero drops into the empty hundreds column, and the answer turns green
phases.does: changes the kilometres part, adds the metres part, and fills the empty column
phases.goal: a zero holds a place open inside the answer, and without it the measure would be far smaller
phases.says: Is any column empty? What goes there?
phases.check: Away from the screen: why does a length of some kilometres and a few metres need a zero in its metres?
phases.feels: a grey zero dropping into the one empty column and the answer settling
phases.hands: Write a length in kilometres and metres where the metres part has only two digits. Change the kilometres, add the metres, and check that every column has a digit.
phases.tries: First rung: change the kilometres part only. Second rung: add a metres part of three digits, with no empty column. Third rung: the same task on one kilometre and a few tens of metres, before the question's own length returns.

wrong.why: the parts look like they just go next to each other
wrong.move: writes the kilometres digit and the two metres digits side by side
wrong.screen: each digit is read back in the column it sits in, showing far fewer metres than the card, and the empty hundreds column is lit amber

wrong.why: a zero somewhere in the number feels like enough
wrong.move: puts the zero after the metres digits instead of in front of them
wrong.screen: each digit is read back from its column, the metres part is shown as far more than the card, and the hundreds column is lit amber

phases.screen: a length in kilometres and metres whose metres part has only two digits
phases.soWhat: a zero holds a place open inside the answer, and without it the measure would be far smaller
phases.concept: A zero that holds a place

phases.win: three grey zeros drop in, and a second sign reads the length in metres, still with the word over, in green
phases.does: drags the want pin to m and hops the point three places right
phases.goal: a length of over 4112 km is over 41,12,000 m, found by three places to the right; the road box prints no question, so this is our own question
phases.says: Our own question. How long is the road in metres?
phases.check: Away from the screen: this is our own question, since the road box prints no question. Why is the answer over a number, not exactly it?
phases.feels: a long road turning into an even longer number that still says over
phases.hands: Write the road's length in kilometres on the paper chart with the word over beside it, move the point three places right, and write the new sign with the word over again.
phases.tries: First rung: hop the road's length one place, into hectometres. Second rung: one more, into decametres. Third rung: the same task on a short road of a few kilometres, before the question's own road returns.

wrong.why: hecto and deca are easy to skip, so kilometres to metres feels shorter than it is
wrong.move: hops the point only two places right
wrong.screen: the point stays and the length is read back in decametres, while the metres column and the one hop still to make are lit amber

wrong.why: a long row of zeros is easy to lose count of
wrong.move: types the length in metres with one zero too few
wrong.screen: the columns the point passed light one at a time, and the one left empty is lit amber inside the child's answer

phases.screen: the length row with a road sign reading over 4112 km, the have pin on km
phases.soWhat: a long length in kilometres is found in metres by three places to the right, and over stays with it

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, as the third hop lands, three grey zeros drop in one after another like counters, and the second road sign swings down beside the first with the length in metres.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet hopped. On the first phase a weight in hectograms sits in the row with the have pin on hectograms and the want pin loose. On the second a capacity's litres part sits in the row and its millilitres part waits on a card beside it. On the third a length's kilometres part sits in the row and its metres part, only two digits long, waits on a card. On the fourth the length row lies under a road sign that reads the road's length in kilometres, with the word over before it. One thing moves, once: the want pin gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any measure set on any row, pinned and hopped right to any smaller unit, with mixed measures added part by part. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on places to the right, mixed measures in the smaller unit, zeros that hold places, and the road.

observations.why: a smaller unit needs more of itself to make the same measure.
observations.soWhat: moving to a smaller unit multiplies the number by 10 for each place.
observations.observe: Each hop to the right made the number bigger, but the measure on the card stayed the same.

observations.why: each column the point passes is one unit of the chart, and it must hold a digit.
observations.soWhat: the zeros are part of the answer, not decoration.
observations.observe: Grey zeros dropped in behind the digits as the point hopped past empty columns.

observations.why: the two parts are in different units until the bigger part is changed.
observations.soWhat: change the bigger part first, then add the smaller part.
observations.observe: The litres part hopped first, and only then did the millilitres slide in beside it.

observations.why: changing the unit changes the number, not what we know about the road.
observations.soWhat: a word like over or about stays with the measure in any unit.
observations.observe: The second road sign still read over.

model.rule: count the places from the unit you have to the unit you want; each place to the right multiplies the number by 10; a mixed measure: the bigger part first, then add the smaller part; a zero holds an empty place

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The pins light amber, the point hops right one place at a time with × 10 under each hop, grey zeros fill the empty columns, and the answer shows in green.
Phase 2: The bigger part hops into the smaller unit one place at a time, the smaller part's card slides into its columns, and the answer shows in green.
Phase 3: The bigger part hops into the smaller unit, the smaller part slides in, the empty column lights amber and a grey zero drops into it, and the answer shows in green.
Phase 4: The point hops the road's length right one place at a time with × 10 under each hop, grey zeros fill the empty columns, and a second sign reads the length in green, still with over.

voice.opening: A measure on the chart, and a pin on its unit.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: pin any unit to the right and hop the point there.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You hopped right to a smaller unit and kept every place.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
